LookaheadSourceTokens.quote: If the phrase “[lookahead = _seq_]” appears in the right-hand side of a production, it indicates that the production may only be used if the token sequence _seq_ is a prefix of the immediately following input token sequence.
These situations are described by saying that semicolons are automatically inserted into the source code token stream in those situations.

notes: "the |X| of _n_" names a child of _n_ (§5.1.2 gives a node only its right-hand side's children), so IsLabelledFunction 1-2 never find the |LabelledStatement| under a |Statement| node: read by §5.1.2 alone, step 1 returns *false* for every |Statement| node and `if (1) l: function f() {}` is valid; test262's labelled-fn-stmt*.js require a SyntaxError. The model reads "_n_ is a |X|" through the unit chain (decisions.md, child-of-through-unit-chain), so its literal reading passes step 1 and stops (a sort error) at step 2, where _n_'s production has no |X|. The test262 and proposed reading: |X| is taken from the first node of _n_'s unit chain whose production has one.

alts.text: It is a Syntax Error if the StringValue of |IdentifierName| is the String value of any terminal of |ReservedWord| except for `yield` or `await`.
It is a Syntax Error if the StringValue of |IdentifierName| is the String value of any terminal of |ReservedWord| except for `yield` or `await`.

notes: "the StringValue of any |ReservedWord| except for `yield` or `await`" takes the StringValue of a |ReservedWord|, for which StringValue has no row. The literal text stops there. The test262 and proposed reading: the StringValue of a terminal is the String value of its code points (test262's val-*-via-escape-*.js require a SyntaxError for an |IdentifierName| that spells a reserved word with escapes).

A lookahead restriction reads "the immediately following input token sequence" (§5.1.6.7), and §12.10 inserts semicolons "into the source code token stream": the text does not say whether an inserted semicolon is a token a lookahead reads. Read as one, `if (0) let` LF `[a] = 0;` is a sentence. The literal text stops wherever a lookahead reads at an inserted semicolon. The test262 and proposed reading: a lookahead reads the source's tokens, past the semicolons §12.10 inserted (test262's let-array-with-newline.js require a SyntaxError).

B.1.1 adds |HTMLCloseComment| as an alternative of |InputElementHashbangOrRegExp| of its own, not under |Comment|, and §5.1.3 drops only white space and comments from the input elements: literally a first-line `-->` is a token that no syntactic production has, and the |Script| has no parse (a SyntaxError). The test262 and proposed reading: an |HTMLCloseComment| input element is a comment (test262's single-line-html-close-first-line-{1,2,3}.js).

B.1.2's "each alternative is considered only if previous production alternatives do not match" says neither what an alternative matches nor how nested choices combine, and without an order its grammar is ambiguous (`/a{1}/`, `/\b*/`, `/\1/`). The literal text stops on a pattern with more than one parse. The test262 and proposed reading: commitment: a node of a nonterminal B.1.2 restates uses an alternative only if no earlier alternative of it derives any span from the node's start (tc39/ecma262 #2228; test262's annexB/built-ins/RegExp).

B.1.2's condition on `AtomEscape :: DecimalEscape`, "the CapturingGroupNumber of |DecimalEscape| is ≤ CountLeftCapturingParensWithin(the |Pattern| containing |DecimalEscape|)", reads the |Pattern| whose parse the condition itself decides. The literal text stops on a pattern with more than one parse. The test262 and proposed reading: stratified: the count is that of a committed parse of the input as Pattern[~UnicodeMode, ~UnicodeSetsMode, ~NamedCaptureGroups] with the condition true (test262's legacy-octal-escape.js).

notes: §22.2.1.1's modifier rules are on |Atom|'s productions; under B.1.2's grammar `(?ii:a)` is an |ExtendedAtom|, for which B.1.2.1 adds no such rule, so literally `/(?ii:a)/`, `/(?-:a)/` and `/(?i-i:a)/` are valid patterns without the u or v flag on a B.1.2 host. The test262 and proposed reading: §22.2.1.1's rules of the two modifier productions of |Atom| apply to the |ExtendedAtom| productions with the same right-hand sides.

§5.1.5 reparses a cover with _n_ as goal, so the covered node roots a tree of its own: "contained within", "most closely contains" and "the parent of" (IsInTailPosition 2, MightBothParticipate 1, ShallowestContainedJSONValue 6.d) fail for a node inside it, and read literally `return (f(n - 1))` is no tail call. The test262 and proposed reading: the covered node takes the cover's place in the tree, its parent being the cover's parent (test262's tco-pos.js).

The proposed reading clamps the text's own difference at zero, so that _now_ + _delay_ is 𝔽([[TimeoutTime]]) whenever the delay is positive: the Job runs no earlier than that time value, which is what AtomicsWaitAsyncTimeoutAssert's proposed Assert needs. Clamping the exact difference instead (𝔽(max([[TimeoutTime]] - ℝ(_now_), 0))) can round the delay down across a millisecond that 𝔽([[TimeoutTime]]) rounds up to.

notes: The literal step passes a List of code units to CreateArrayFromList, whose parameter is a List of ECMAScript language values; a code unit is not one. test262 requires the Array's elements to be the Strings of one code unit each (built-ins/String/prototype/split/separator-empty-string-instance-is-string.js), as the method's description says: "any _separator_ coerced to the empty String splits the *this* value into individual code units".

Step 1.a of Races (sec-races) is always true: an execution's happens-before is a strict partial order, so _eventA_ and _eventB_ never both happen-before each other, and any two conflicting events race. The memory model's meaning (Ecma.MemoryModel.Race) reads the literal text. The proposed text of step 1.a: "If neither _eventA_ happens-before _eventB_ in _execution_ nor _eventB_ happens-before _eventA_ in _execution_, then".

The third condition of happens-before orders an ~init~ write only before events whose memory ranges are *overlapping*, and "overlapping" excludes equal ranges, so a 1-byte event at an ~init~ event's byte is not ordered after it. The proposed text: "SharedDataBlockEventSet(_execution_) contains both _eventA_ and _eventB_, _eventA_.[[Order]] is ~init~, _eventA_ and _eventB_ are not the same Shared Data Block event, and _eventA_ and _eventB_ do not have disjoint memory ranges."

A memory range is a Set of integers, the byte indices from [[ByteIndex]], with no [[Block]] in it, so reads-bytes-from's "has _readEvent_.[[ByteIndex]] + _i_ in its memory range" and coherent reads' "has _byteLocation_ in its memory range" (step 1.c.ii) admit a write to another Shared Data Block at the same index. The proposed text, which the memory model's meaning (Ecma.MemoryModel.Rbf.Valid, CoherentReads) reads: "Each event _writeEvent_ with index _i_ in _writes_ has _readEvent_.[[Block]] as its [[Block]] and _readEvent_.[[ByteIndex]] + _i_ in its memory range", and in step 1.c.ii "a WriteSharedMemory or ReadModifyWriteSharedMemory event _value_ whose [[Block]] is _readEvent_.[[Block]] and that has _byteLocation_ in its memory range".

1. Let _cells_ be a copy of _finalizationRegistry_.[[Cells]].
        1. For each Record { [[WeakRefTarget]], [[HeldValue]], [[UnregisterToken]] } _cell_ of _cells_, do
          1. If _cell_.[[UnregisterToken]] is not ~empty~ and SameValue(_cell_.[[UnregisterToken]], _unregisterToken_) is *true*, then
            1. Remove _cell_ from _finalizationRegistry_.[[Cells]].
            1. Set _removed_ to *true*.

notes: The literal step removes from the List it iterates, and the For each convention does not say which element comes next; read literally, the cell after a removed one is skipped. test262 requires every cell with the token to go (built-ins/FinalizationRegistry/prototype/unregister/unregister-object-token.js and unregister-symbol-token.js register two cells with one token in a row). The proposed text iterates a copy, as above.

alts.text: 1. Return *false*.

notes: IsCharacterClass has no definition for this production of §B.1.2, whose CharacterValue §B.1.2.4 gives, and §B.1.2.1's range rules ask for it of every |ClassAtom| of a range: `/[\c1-\c5]/`. The literal text stops there (it asks IsCharacterClass of |ClassControlLetter|, which has no definition either). The row is the twin of <emu-grammar>ClassEscape :: CharacterEscape</emu-grammar>'s: the escape is one character. No test262 test has `\c` and a digit or `_` at a range's end; annexB/language/literals/regexp/class-escape.js reads `[\c1]` as U+0011.

alts.text:
1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"exponentiate"*, _base_, _exponent_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _base_ raised to the power _exponent_.

1. If _x_ is *0*<sub>ℤ</sub> or _y_ is *0*<sub>ℤ</sub>, return _x_.
        1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"leftShift"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ × *2*<sub>ℤ</sub><sup>_y_</sup>.

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"multiply"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ × _y_.

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"add"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ + _y_.

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"subtract"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ - _y_.

1. If _bits_ = 0 or _bigint_ is *0*<sub>ℤ</sub>, return *0*<sub>ℤ</sub>.
        1. If _bigint_ > *0*<sub>ℤ</sub> and _bits_ ≥ 4 × (DecimalExponent(ℝ(_bigint_)) + 1), return _bigint_.
        1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"asUintN"*, _bigint_, ℤ(_bits_)) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return ℤ(ℝ(_bigint_) modulo 2<sup>_bits_</sup>).

notes: §6.1.6.2 says a BigInt "may be any size and is not limited to a particular bit-width", and BigInt::exponentiate, BigInt::leftShift, BigInt::multiply, BigInt::add, BigInt::subtract and BigInt.asUintN return their exact results whatever their size; every implementation has a maximum size and throws a *RangeError* past it (V8 at 2<sup>30</sup> bits). The proposed text, in each of the six before its result is formed: "If the result would exceed the implementation's maximum BigInt size, throw a *RangeError* exception." The host says whether it would (BigIntTooLarge). The literal text forms the result whatever its size, so an implementation gives up at a limit of its own. Not a defect of the text: a proposed normative change, which says what every implementation does (docs/spec-issues/51-bigint-maximum-size.md).

alts.text:
1. If StringTooLarge(_n_ × the length of _string_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return the String value that is made from _n_ copies of _string_ appended together.

1. If _fillString_ is not the empty String and StringTooLarge(_intMaxLength_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return StringPad(_string_, _intMaxLength_, _fillString_, _placement_).

1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _result_ + the length of _nextString_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Set _result_ to the string-concatenation of _result_ and _nextString_.

1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _leftString_ + the length of _rightString_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return the string-concatenation of _leftString_ and _rightString_.

1. If _k_ > 0, then
          1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _result_ + the length of _separator_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
          1. Set _result_ to the string-concatenation of _result_ and _separator_.

1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _result_ + the length of _elementString_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Set _result_ to the string-concatenation of _result_ and _elementString_.

notes: §6.1.4 defines the String type as sequences of up to 2<sup>53</sup> - 1 16-bit code units and leaves the operations' behaviour unspecified when a result would exceed an implementation's smaller maximum String length; every engine throws a *RangeError* past its limit (V8 2<sup>28</sup> on 32-bit targets and 2<sup>29</sup> - 24 on 64-bit, SpiderMonkey 2<sup>30</sup> - 2, JavaScriptCore 2<sup>31</sup> - 1). The proposed text checks StringTooLarge before constructing the String and throws a *RangeError* exception when *true* (docs/spec-issues/53-string-maximum-length.md).

§12.9.3 defines |DecimalIntegerLiteral| as "|DecimalDigit|", "|NonZeroDigit| |NumericLiteralSeparator|? |DecimalDigits|[+Sep]" and "|NonOctalDecimalIntegerLiteral|", and has no production <emu-grammar>DecimalIntegerLiteral :: `0`</emu-grammar>; §12.9.3.2 MV still has the row "The MV of <emu-grammar>DecimalIntegerLiteral :: `0`</emu-grammar> is 0." The row names no production of the grammar, so it is never applied: the MV of the literal `0` is that of <emu-grammar>DecimalIntegerLiteral :: DecimalDigit</emu-grammar>, the MV of its |DecimalDigit|, which is 0. Both readings agree. The proposed text: delete the row (docs/spec-issues/52-mv-decimalintegerliteral-zero.md).
